subject: Priority ranking ops recap + unanswered evaluation items
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@clearpathhealth.com>, Michael Green <michael.green@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Priority ranking ops recap + unanswered evaluation items

Lydia / Michael — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can converge on an integration plan for the reranker/pass-two architecture: 

Recap (what we heard)
- You want a two-stage pipeline: lightweight embed+approx search (first pass) -> reranker as a secondary scoring pass for top results.
- Latency target: P95 end-to-end for query = 250ms (95ms budget for reranker).
- Typical query mix: 60% short queries (<=8 tokens), 40% long/context queries (up to 256 tokens).
- Index size: ~120M documents, expect 10M active candidates for cold starts; typical top candidate set for rerank = 50.

Open questions we flagged during call (please confirm priorities):
1) Auth model for the private environment — API keys vs mTLS vs customer-managed KMS for model keys?
2) Routing policy: prefer regional routing (us-east) with fallback to a lower-cost model variant if capacity is constrained — acceptable?
3) Acceptance criteria for reranker quality: which offline metrics matter (nDCG@10, MRR, pairwise accuracy)?
4) Top_k tuning: initial suggestion was k=50 but unclear if you'll accept the cost/latency trade for k=50 vs k=20.
5) Evaluation dataset: do you have a labeled relevance set we can use, or should we run an A/B with human-in-the-loop judgments?

Proposed short plan (what we'll do next)
- Aisha will draft an eval harness spec (attached) and a sample SDK auth snippet for your infra.
- We propose a two-week pilot: offline eval on your labeled set (if available) + a 2-week canary with k=20 then k=50 to compare quality vs latency.
- Deliverables: eval-harness-spec.md, sample-queries.csv (small sample), suggested routing policy + cost estimate.

Attachments: eval-harness-spec.md (detailed test plan), sample-queries.csv (50 sample queries), architecture-diagram.png

Next steps (ask):
- Lydia: confirm whether you can share a small labeled set (2k queries) or if we should plan for human annotations.
- Michael: confirm latency SLO flexibility (can reranker be allowed up to 120ms for warm caches?).
- Internal: Aisha / Ben — can you sketch the proposed SDK auth snippets and a simple flow for reranker fallback?

I'll book a 30-minute follow-up for next Tuesday; please add items to the agenda if you want other owners looped in.

— Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — useful summary. A few clarifications on our side: 

1) Labeled set: we have an internal relevance pool (~1.2k human-labeled queries) but it's not stratified by recency. We can share a de-identified sample of ~1k queries for offline eval next week.
2) Latency: the 250ms P95 is firm for customer-facing UI; for background/analytics endpoints we can tolerate higher latency. For the reranker specifically, we can push to 120ms p95 for warm cache but prefer <100ms for steady-state.
3) Top_k: cost sensitivity means we want k=20 as the default, with experiments for k=40/60 for narrow slices (e.g., content-rich queries).
4) Auth: security prefers mutual TLS inside our private VPC; however, for the hosted POC we can accept API keys if you support scoped keys and per-route policies.

Open Q: can Redwood produce a quick estimate for cost delta between k=20 and k=50 on the dataset size above? Also we'd like to see the evaluation script you'll use (metrics + significance test).

I can join the follow-up next Tuesday — please share the calendar invite.

— Lydia Park

Thanks — a few engineering notes and a concrete evaluation proposal from our side.

Auth and SDK
- For the POC: scoped API keys (per-route + timeboxed) are the fastest to get started. We'll include a rotation script. For Private/VPC: we support mTLS and customer-managed KMS for model encryption. We'll include an auth decision matrix in the spec.

Routing and model variants
- Recommend primary routing to us-east-1 cluster with an immediate fallback to a cheaper fp16-quantized variant if queue depth > 75%. Fallback keeps same API contract (same shape) so UI code doesn't change.

Top_k tuning and latency planning
- Baseline numbers (estimate for your mix & index size): reranker per-item cost approx 6ms/token on A100-style nodes with kv-cache hit. For short queries (avg 8 tokens) + k=20, expected extra latency ~ 80-100ms (warm). For k=50, expected ~ 160-200ms. These match your SLO constraints: k=20 is a safe default; k=50 will require either larger GPU allocation or batching adjustments.

Evaluation metrics and statistical tests
- We'll run offline metrics: nDCG@10, MRR@10, Precision@k, pairwise accuracy, and Kendall tau for ranking correlation.
- For significance: we use bootstrap confidence intervals + paired t-test on paired-query scores (recommend bootstrap for nDCG). We'll deliver the evaluation script and the Jupyter notebook.

Pilot plan (concrete)
1) You provide: de-identified 1k labeled queries + expected click/satisfaction proxy (if available).
2) Redwood runs: offline eval comparing baseline (approx search only) vs reranker at k in {10,20,50}.
3) Run significance tests and produce a signal matrix that maps metric deltas to quality tags (e.g., delta nDCG@10 > 0.03 -> material).
4) Canary: 2-week canary with k=20 (50% traffic) then a 1-week spike test for k=50 on a small slice.

SDK snippet (pseudo):
- POST /v1/ranking:
  headers: { Authorization: "Bearer <SCOPED_KEY>", "X-Region": "us-east-1" }
  body: { query: "...", candidate_ids: [..], reranker: { model: "rdw-ranker-v2", top_k: 20, structured_output: true } }

We'll attach the eval-harness-spec.md (draft) and a small sample-queries.csv to this thread. Ben will follow up with a cost delta estimate between k=20 and k=50 for the size you quoted.

If that plan sounds good I'll queue the offline run as soon as we get the labeled set.

— Aisha Rahman
